messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: METRICS > billing_metering_aggregation_delay critical
Alert ID: PD-5429
Service: billing-metering-pipeline
Symptom: hourly aggregation lag > 45m (tokens undercounted)
Triggered at: 2026-03-14T22:21:36Z

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alert PD-5429 fired and routed to devon (oncall).

devon (oncall): ack'd. seeing the same in CloudWatch — aggregation lag spike around 22:05 UTC. Investigating.

carmen (sre): @devon can you confirm whether downstream invoice export has already run for this hour? if so we need to pause exports to avoid bad invoices.

devon (oncall): Export job schedule is cron: 23 * * * * UTC — next run in ~39m. but the aggregator is reporting ~3h behind for a subset of shards.

jess (eng-ml): :eyes: I can look at the aggregator worker logs. Possible KV cache eviction bug we saw in staging last month.

ops-runner-bot: Running quick diagnostic: kubectl exec -n metering metering-aggregator-0 -- /bin/sh -c "ps aux | grep aggregator"
ops-runner-bot: Running tail of logs (last 200 lines):
```
2026-03-14T22:03:18Z INFO fetcher shard=13 fetched 0 rows from cursor
2026-03-14T22:04:01Z WARN compactor shard=7 backpressure=true queue=98
2026-03-14T22:05:02Z ERROR aggregator shard=3 token_count_mismatch expected=124512 actual=0
2026-03-14T22:06:00Z INFO aggregator evicted_kv_entries=243
2026-03-14T22:07:11Z ERROR aggregator shard=12 fetch_timeout
```

carmen (sre): that ERROR line for token_count_mismatch is bad — suggests upstream read/merge failed for those shards. we should block invoice export and notify revenue ops immediately.

alex (revenueops): on it. please set pause_export=true on the billing-export service and open a manual invoice hold for today. Don't send any invoices until we confirm counts.

devon (oncall): done: 
```
# temporary toggle
kubectl -n billing patch deployment billing-export --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"pause_export":"true"}}}}}'
```
Export paused. Posted note in billing-runbook.

jess (eng-ml): running targeted query to compare aggregator vs raw events for the last 6 hours:
```
SELECT hour, sum(token_count) as agg_tokens
FROM usage_aggregates
WHERE hour >= '2026-03-14 16:00:00'::timestamp
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 6;
```
Got back:
```
hour                | agg_tokens
2026-03-14 22:00:00 | 0
2026-03-14 21:00:00 | 312394
2026-03-14 20:00:00 | 298201
```
Then raw events:
```
SELECT hour, count(*) as raw_rows, sum(token_count) as raw_tokens
FROM raw_usage_events
WHERE hour >= '2026-03-14 16:00:00'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 6;
```
Raw shows 22:00 hour ~315k tokens. So aggregator missing whole hour for many shards.

liam (product): customer-impact check: which customers are affected? any enterprise invoices due tomorrow?

jess (eng-ml): join query to get top accounts by tokens in that hour -> top 5 accounts would be impacted (acct_874, acct_1023, acct_44, acct_9001, acct_112). I'll DM revenueops the list.

alex (revenueops): got the list. I'll reach out to account reps + set manual holds for the top 10. Also escalating to legal for any contract obligations.

carmen (sre): quick triage: seems to be an aggregator merge path where KV cache eviction + retry path drops shard state if the fetch returns empty. I can push a hotfix to add a defensive no-op merge to avoid zeroing counts while we backfill. Need eng-ml review.

jess (eng-ml): I can review. Can you open a PR with the patch? we should also start a backfill for the missing window. estimated backfill time for 6h = ~25m on current cluster if we parallelize by shard.

devon (oncall): PR link pls. I'll also start a targeted backfill job: ops-runner-bot, kick job backfill-window=2026-03-14T22:00:00Z..2026-03-14T23:00:00Z shards=all priority=high

ops-runner-bot: Backfill job queued: job_id=bf-2026-03-14-179012. estimated runtime 00:28:00. running on cluster metering-bf-1.

pagerduty: PD: PD-5429 acknowledged by devon (oncall) at 22:22 UTC. After 10m without resolution, escalated to carmen (sre).

carmen (sre): I'm on it. I've applied the hotfix as a canary to aggregator-1 (shard subset) and instrumented extra metrics for fetch_success_rate. patch: https://git.internal/redwood/metering/pull/2895

jess (eng-ml): reviewed and approved. rolling to agg-0..agg-3 canary now. watch for token_count_mismatch logs.

ops-runner-bot: Backfill job bf-2026-03-14-179012 started at 22:31:45Z.

devon (oncall): early results: after hotfix, canary shard merge reports agg_tokens for 22:00 now 314k (matches raw). Backfill progress: 12/64 shards complete.

alex (revenueops): summary for execs: paused invoice export, manual holds on top-10 accounts, notified AEs. We'll prepare customer comms if backfill doesn't finish before invoice run.

liam (product): please capture RCA action items: make the KV eviction path idempotent, add unit test for empty-fetch merge, and add a pre-export sanity check that compares raw vs aggregate counts with a >5% diff guard that blocks exports.

carmen (sre): adding to post-incident ticket INC-2026-03-14-agg-lag.

jess (eng-ml): backfill completed at 22:47:10Z. Verifying aggregates...

ops-runner-bot: Backfill job bf-2026-03-14-179012 finished success in 00:15:23.

jess (eng-ml): verification query shows 22:00 agg_tokens = 315,102 (matches raw within 0.2%). running final sanity diff across last 24h.

devon (oncall): unpaused invoice export at 22:56 (set pause_export=false) — but we left manual holds on affected accounts until revenueops confirms.

alex (revenueops): confirmed manual holds remain for top-10. we'll lift holds after final audit.

carmen (sre): PagerDuty PD-5429 resolved and closed. Root cause: aggregator merge path dropped shard data when a fetch returned empty during KV eviction; deployed hotfix and backfill restored counts.

liam (product): good job. next steps: postmortem, schedule follow-up to add pre-export guard and automated rollback for aggregator canary.

devon (oncall): handing off to carmen for overnight watch — I need to step off at 23:05 UTC. Handoff: all backfills complete, exports unpaused, manual holds still active, runbook link: https://wiki.internal/redwood/metering/incident-runbook#INC-2026-03-14-agg-lag

carmen (sre): taking handoff. I'll monitor fetch_success_rate and set alert threshold tighter for next 24h.

alex (revenueops): I'll send a short customer note to affected accounts saying "potential billing discrepancy detected; invoices are on hold while we reconcile. no action needed from you." Draft here for review: "We're reconciling token counts for [date]; we've placed a temporary hold and will notify when invoices are released."

jess (eng-ml): creating PR for unit test and adding sentinel check in export pipeline. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/metering/pull/2896

carmen (sre): closing thread — monitor for regressions and follow up in INC-2026-03-14. :white_check_mark:
